capabilities: Pair devices with a single-use QR code or pairing link
Sync selected notes, folders, or the whole vault over a LAN
Run a one-time transfer without creating an ongoing sync
Set per-device direction, selected paths, and deletion policy
Back up overwritten or deleted content before the target changes
disambiguation: Not a QR code generator or scanner; QR codes are used only once to pair two devices for local network sync.
extras: Free and open source under the MIT License; in public beta, so the README advises starting with a backup or test vault. Android is not validated or supported, .obsidian is excluded, files over 20 MB are skipped by default, and the host must stay awake with Obsidian open.
problem: Syncing notes between your own devices usually needs a cloud service or account, and Obsidian has no built-in way to copy only chosen notes over a local network.

relations.evidence: LAN Vault Sync, MIT: desktop-host/mobile-client topology and Obsidian protocol QR pairing.
Self-hosted LiveSync: encrypted setup URIs and conflict-handling concepts.
Obsidian Decentralized, GPL-3.0: WebRTC and application-layer encryption were studied

summary: Encrypted LAN sync plugin that pairs devices with a QR code and moves selected notes or folders between Obsidian vaults.
